BiblicalUsage: The sense of rûwsh is to be destitute. In 1 Samuel 18:23, we read, "…Saul's servants spake those words in the ears…"; in 2 Samuel 12:1, "And the LORD sent Nathan unto David. And…". You hear it again in Ecclesiastes 4:14 — "…prison he cometh to reign; whereas also born…" — and in Proverbs 10:4, "He becometh poor that dealeth a slack hand…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rûwsh is the Lord's own word, and it shows his people what he is like. I hold that rûwsh still speaks, because the God who spoke then has not changed.
